items.item_text: International Code Council (ICC) Certified Fire Inspector II and International Code Council (ICC) Certified Fire Plans Examiner.
Employment is subject to a criminal background check and pre-employment physical.
Must be able to work various hours and locations based on business needs.
Emergency Response/On-Call: Must be available to respond to campus fire/life safety emergencies, critical utility impairments, and catastrophic events outside normal business hours as required.

Nine (9) years of progressively responsible professional experience in complex fire prevention, plan review, and code enforcement, with specialized emphasis on healthcare or institutional environments OR Bachelor’s degree in Fire Protection Engineering, Fire Science, Construction Management, Civil/Mechanical Engineering, or related field, plus five (5) years of related experience/training.

Related Experience: Experience in fire prevention work within a public fire prevention bureau, building inspection agency, or in fire prevention/industrial safety engineering within private industry, preferably a minimum of five years.
Healthcare Experience evaluating active OSHPD/HCAI Institutional (I-Occupancy) hospital environments and managing The Joint Commission (TJC) standards.
Experience working within a healthcare or academic medical center setting.

Under the general direction of the Lead Designated Campus Fire Marshal (DCFM), the Assistant Fire Marshal serves as a technical authority, performing complex fire and life safety enforcement, technical plan reviews, and field inspections for UCSD Health’s healthcare facilities, clinics, and research laboratories.

Operating under the delegated authority of the Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between the University of California and the California Office of the State Fire Marshal (OSFM), the incumbent independently reviews, approves, or rejects design and construction documents and enforces California Code of Regulations (CCR) Titles 19 and 24, NFPA standards, and Department of Health Care Access and Information (HCAI) mandates. The position serves as an institutional liaison to local fire authorities, state regulators, and accreditation bodies to ensure continuous hospital readiness and life safety compliance.

Conduct technical plan reviews of complex healthcare facility construction, modifications, and fire protection systems. Ensure structural designs comply with HCAI, California Building Standards Codes (Title 24), Title 19 (Public Safety), NFPA 99 (Health Care Facilities Code), and NFPA 101 (Life Safety Code).
Direct and perform field inspections of new construction, structural modifications, tenant improvements, and infrastructure modernizations across all UCSD Health properties.

Plan, schedule, and conduct mandatory hospital fire and evacuation drills across diverse medical occupancies. Develop and deliver advanced fire prevention and community risk reduction training programs for clinical and research personnel.
Inspect existing facilities for ongoing Title 19 compliance.
Manage, schedule, and evaluate mandatory hospital fire drills across varied clinical shifts and occupancies in accordance with The Joint Commission (TJC), CMS, and Title 19 standards.

Upon receiving OSFM approval, act as the Designated Campus Fire Marshal (DCFM) on behalf of UCSD Health. Utilize delegated authority under the UCOP-OSFM Memorandum of Agreement to review, approve, or deny construction plans, modifications, and fire-life safety infrastructure.

Designated Campus Fire Marshal (DCFM) Requirement: Must be successfully nominated by the University and accepted/approved by the California Office of the State Fire Marshal (OSFM) to hold Designated Campus Fire Marshal (DCFM)authority within 6-12 months of appointment.
HCAI Qualification: possess or be fully qualified to obtain the Department of Health Care Access and Information (HCAI)Fire and Life Safety Officer II (FLSO II).
California State Fire Training (OSFM) Fire Inspector II (formerly Fire Inspector 2A, 2B, 2C, and 2D).
California State Fire Training (OSFM) Fire Plans Examiner.
Thorough knowledge and skill in applying and interpreting applicable local, state, and federal regulations and related standards and guidelines.
Thorough written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, including political acumen and skill to communicate effectively in a diverse environment.
Strong analytical and organizational skills to organize, prioritize and manage the successful completion of projects within time and budget constraints.
